environment.images: All eight application images rebuilt from this checkout using docker compose build
environment.data: Dedicated fresh PostgreSQL and Kafka volumes; existing application data was not migrated or reconciled

scenarios.method: Existing scripts/e2e-concurrency.sh through Gateway against real PostgreSQL and Kafka
assertions: Two concurrent trip creation requests both returned HTTP 201 with distinct trip IDs
Exactly one trip ASSIGNED to the sole candidate; other trip SEARCHING without a driver at the acceptance snapshot
Driver BUSY; database reserved_for_trip equals the winner trip ID

scenarios.method: Create, assign, accept and start a real trip through Gateway; stop Payment before completing that trip
assertions: Payment container reached stopped state before trip completion
The trip completed successfully while Payment was stopped
Trip remained COMPLETED; no payment row existed before restart
The real TripCompleted event was readable from Kafka while Payment was stopped
Payment consumer group had no active members and lag 2 on trip-events partition 0
An additional assigned trip was cancelled through Gateway
Cancellation recorded exactly one SAGA_COMPENSATED entry and released the driver to AVAILABLE with no reserved_for_trip

scenarios.method: Restart Payment and poll the original trip through Gateway without publishing a replacement event
assertions: Exactly one SUCCESS payment row existed and its amount matched the final fare
Payment consumer lag returned to zero on partitions with records

limitations: Scenario 8 permits retry, queue handling OR compensation; this run demonstrated queue handling AND cancellation compensation, not retry exhaustion or DLQ replay
This run does not validate cutover or migration of the existing W3 application volumes
The scenario 6 snapshot verifies exclusive assignment; it does not require the unsuccessful trip to be rejected synchronously at creation
artifacts: Raw transcripts, Kafka offsets, image IDs and final Trip DB snapshot are in this directory. Temporary runner/configuration is under ignored build/acceptance; the resolved compose configuration is not published because it contains environment credentials.
